title: PWM starts off, status reports it, and 'off' releases the claw
preconditions: Claw serial test image flashed (separate opt-in build), claw empty, wheels clear, terminal open on the Pico COM port
steps: Wait for the banner 'GP13 CLAW TEST; wheels and mission disabled; PWM off'. Send status, then claw 35, then off
expected: status replies 'PWM off'; claw 35 replies 'OK commanded 35 deg; PWM off after 2 s'; off replies 'OK PWM off' and the claw goes limp

title: Valid angles 0 to 180 are accepted and the PWM drops after 2 s
preconditions: As CLAW-001
steps: Send claw 35, claw 40, claw 45 one at a time, then status right after one of them
expected: Each replies 'OK commanded N deg; PWM off after 2 s' and the claw moves a little; status replies 'Commanded N deg (not measured)'; PWM stops by itself after 2 s

title: Invalid input is rejected and does not move the claw
preconditions: As CLAW-001
steps: Send claw 200, claw abc, CLAW 35 (capital letters) and a line longer than 24 characters
expected: The first three reply 'ERR use claw 0..180, status, or off'; the long line replies 'ERR invalid or too-long line'; the claw does not move

title: open and close in the mission build use the mission angles
preconditions: Mission build flashed, state IDLE, claw empty, wheels clear
steps: Send open, then close, over Wi-Fi or USB
expected: open drives the claw to 30 degrees and close to 50 degrees (CLAW_OPEN_DEG, CLAW_CLOSE_DEG); both are refused while the mission is running or stopped

title: Camera report frames carry an XOR checksum and bad frames are rejected
preconditions: XIAO connected over UART; frames look like 'A,...*XX' where XX is the XOR of the payload bytes in hex
steps: Send the Pico a frame with a wrong or missing checksum (for example '*00' or no '*')
expected: camera_validate_frame returns false and the frame is dropped; no marker is stored and the mission is unaffected

title: ArUco 4x4 markers are detected at the working distance
preconditions: Marker about 80 mm, flat, well lit
steps: Hold marker ID 1 in view and read the camera monitor
expected: Monitor prints 'ArUco scan: 1 marker(s), first ID 1, size 80 mm'

title: Mission waits in IDLE until start
preconditions: Build with MISSION_WAIT_FOR_START=1
expected: state: IDLE, wheels do not move
evidence: status: state: IDLE

title: Mapping sweep turns a full circle in 15-degree steps
preconditions: Robot on the floor, IMU OK, camera connected
steps: Send start and watch '[map] scanning at N degrees'
expected: Turns about 360 degrees with a pause at each step
evidence: Turn angle about -358 degrees recorded; per-step log lines were not captured

title: No usable direction marker stops the mission
preconditions: Only a marker with ID 0 in view
expected: '[map] sweep complete; mapped 0/3', 'Not enough direction markers mapped', STOPPED
evidence: status: stop: Not enough direction markers mapped

title: Only marker IDs 1 to 3 count as direction markers
preconditions: ID 0 marker in view
expected: ID 0 is ignored; mapped count stays 0
evidence: ID 0 marker gave mapped 0, matching the code (direction IDs 1 to 3, objects 4 and up)

title: Mapping succeeds with direction markers 1 to 3
preconditions: ArUco 4x4 markers ID 1 to 3, about 80 mm, in view
expected: '[map] sweep complete; mapped N/3 (N at least 1)', then '[mission] ENABLED: direction map ready'
evidence: Operator said everything works after replacing the marker

title: Robot picks up an object and delivers it
preconditions: Object marker ID 4 or higher placed, direction map ready
expected: Gripping, delivery to a direction marker, delivered count increases
evidence: Operator said everything works; no log captured

title: stop during a run, then reset and start, recovers
preconditions: Mission running
expected: Motors stop, reset returns IDLE, start begins a new sweep

title: IMU start-up check passes on a still robot
preconditions: Robot flat and untouched for about 25 s after power-up
steps: Power on and watch the IMU lines
expected: G_Hz10 stays inside 900 to 1100 (about 1000) with the gyro still, held for 2000 ms within 60 s; no STOP LATCHED; status shows imu: OK
evidence: G_Hz10=1000 on the merged build; status: imu: OK

title: Start-up check fails when the robot is disturbed
preconditions: Robot handled or shaken during calibration
steps: Power on and move the robot
expected: 'Gyro calibration too noisy on axis N' (variance above 1.0 on an axis over 200 samples), FAULT -57, STOP LATCHED, power cycle needed
status: Observed - safety stop worked as designed
evidence: Log: Gyro calibration too noisy on axis 1 / Fault -57 / STOP LATCHED: IMU startup checks failed

title: Start-up check fails when the gyro rate is wrong
preconditions: Cold power-up on a build without the clock fix
expected: 'IMU readiness timed out' and STOP LATCHED
status: Observed - safety stop worked as designed
evidence: G_Hz10=1948, then: [startup] IMU readiness timed out.

title: Missing IMU is reported as a fault
preconditions: Pico with no IMU attached
expected: FAULT=-57 and STOP LATCHED
status: Observed - safety stop worked as designed
evidence: Spare Pico without an IMU showed FAULT=-57 and stayed stopped

title: Motion is refused while stopped or when the IMU is unhealthy
preconditions: IMU fault or stale data
steps: Send start or a manual drive command
expected: Rejected, wheels do not move
status: Observed - safety stop worked as designed
evidence: start rejected repeatedly with 'IMU fault or stale gyro data' even after reset

title: Gyro data older than 50 ms stops the robot
preconditions: Mission running
steps: Delay or block the IMU task
expected: Reading becomes invalid and a stop is latched ('IMU fault or stale gyro data')

title: MPU-6500 (WHO_AM_I 0x70) is accepted
preconditions: MPU-6500 on I2C1 address 0x68
expected: '[MPU] WHO_AM_I=0x70' and start-up continues (0x71, MPU-9250, is also accepted; any other ID is 'Unsupported device ID')
evidence: WHO_AM_I=0x70 printed and calibration started

title: Claw signal stays idle at boot
preconditions: Power on
expected: '[init] gripper PWM ready; signal idle until an object marker is detected'
evidence: Line printed on every boot

title: IMU start-up passes with the camera board connected
preconditions: XIAO connected
steps: Power on with and without the XIAO connected
expected: Start-up check passes either way
evidence: Plain servo-control build failed 'too noisy' with the XIAO attached and passed once without it. That build also lacked the clock fix, so the XIAO is not proven to be the cause. Retest with the merged build

title: start releases the mission from IDLE
preconditions: State IDLE, IMU OK
expected: Mission begins with the 360-degree mapping sweep
evidence: After start the robot turned about 358 degrees (status: turned -359 deg since start-up)

title: start is refused while stopped
preconditions: A stop is latched
expected: Reply 'rejected: stopped (<reason>); type reset'
evidence: rejected: stopped (IMU fault or stale gyro data); type reset

title: reset clears a latched stop and returns to IDLE
preconditions: A stop is latched and the mission task has parked or ended
expected: Reply 'ok: reset, IDLE (type start)'
evidence: ok: reset, IDLE (type start)

title: stop halts the motors at any time
preconditions: Wheels lifted, mission running or manual move in progress
expected: Wheels brake within the drive task's next check (design: 10 ms or less) and the mission parks

expected: Accepted as CMD_START (a=0, b=0, c=0)
evidence: Reply text: "ok: start"

evidence: Reply text: "ok: stop"

title: Parser: "reset"
preconditions: Host PC, cli.c built with CLI_ENABLE_MANUAL=1
expected: Accepted as CMD_RESET (a=0, b=0, c=0)
evidence: Reply text: "ok: reset"

expected: Accepted as CMD_STATUS (a=0, b=0, c=0)
evidence: No reply text (as expected)

preconditions: Host PC, cli.c built with CLI_ENABLE_MANUAL=1
expected: Accepted as CMD_DRIVE (a=30, b=30, c=500)
evidence: Reply text: "ok: drive L=30 R=30 500 ms"

title: Parser: "drive 40 -60 800"

expected: Accepted as CMD_DRIVE (a=40, b=-60, c=800)
evidence: Reply text: "ok: drive L=40 R=-60 800 ms"

title: Parser: "claw 90"
preconditions: Host PC, cli.c built with CLI_ENABLE_MANUAL=1
expected: Accepted as CMD_CLAW (a=90, b=0, c=0)
evidence: Reply text: "ok: claw 90 deg"

title: Parser: "fly"
preconditions: Host PC, cli.c built with CLI_ENABLE_MANUAL=1
expected: Rejected with CLI_ERR_UNKNOWN
evidence: Reply text: "error: unknown command 'fly' (try: help)"

title: Parser: "f 101"
preconditions: Host PC, cli.c built with CLI_ENABLE_MANUAL=1
expected: Rejected with CLI_ERR_VALUE
evidence: Reply text: "error: speed '101' must be 1-100"

title: Line editor: too long
preconditions: Host PC, cli.c built
steps: Feed the typed characters for 'too long' through cli_line_feed()
expected: Final feed result CLI_FEED_TOO_LONG

title: Joins the phone hotspot and gets an IP address (warm boot)
preconditions: Hotspot on and awake, 2.4 GHz, credentials built in
steps: Flash the Wi-Fi build, power on, run the log receiver
expected: Receiver shows [Pico 172.20.10.N] lines; Pico has an address in the hotspot subnet
evidence: Pico appeared at 172.20.10.9 and 172.20.10.11 in the receiver

title: Joins from a cold start on a power bank (3 runs)
preconditions: Pico unplugged from laptop, powered only by power bank, robot still
steps: Unplug fully, plug into power bank, time until the LED is solid, then send status. Repeat 3 times
expected: Joins within about 15 s each time and status is answered
evidence: Join times: 10 s, 15 s, 10 s. status answered 3/3

title: DHCP lease is obtained and the command listener starts after it
preconditions: As WIFI-001
steps: Watch the USB or Wi-Fi log after the join
expected: Progress lines '[wifi] joined, waiting for IP', then '[wifi-log] own ...' and '[cmd] listening for commands on UDP port 5006'
evidence: Log showed dhcp_elapsed=3019 ms and 6039 ms, then own 172.20.10.9 and the listening line

title: Clock tick is correct after a cold power-up (IMU rate about 1000)
preconditions: cpu_clock.c includes the WATCHDOG_TICK write
steps: Unplug fully, power on, read the IMU line G_Hz10
expected: G_Hz10 is about 1000 on cold starts (accepted window 900 to 1100)
evidence: With the fix: 1000 on 3 of 3 cold starts, and on a cold start of the merged Wi-Fi build. Without the fix (plain servo-control build): 1948 on a cold start and the start-up check timed out

title: Wi-Fi credentials are not stored in the repository
preconditions: robot-arm-main source tree
steps: Check third_party/mtk3smp-rp2040/.gitignore and search tracked files for real SSID/password definitions
expected: config/wifi_credentials.h and config/wifi_log_config.h are ignored; only *.example.h and setup_wifi.py contain placeholders
evidence: Ignored files listed on lines 16-17; only 'replace-with-ssid' / 'replace-with-password' placeholders found

title: Status over Wi-Fi returns state, stop reason and IMU health
preconditions: Pico joined the hotspot, has an IP, mission task running, laptop on the same hotspot
expected: Reply has three lines: state, stop reason, imu OK/NOT READY
evidence: Reply: state: IDLE  holding: -  delivered: 0 / stop: none / imu: OK  turned 94 deg since start-up

title: Reply is sent back to the laptop that sent the command
preconditions: As CMD-001
steps: Send a command from the laptop console (tools/wifi_cli.py)
expected: The answer appears in that same console, not only in the log
evidence: Console showed 'ok: reset, IDLE (type start)' and 'rejected: ...' replies
source: third_party/mtk3smp-rp2040/lib/libwifi/sysdepend/pico_rp2040/cyw43_utk.c (robot_cmd_recv: udp_sendto to the sender's address and port)

title: Input longer than 64 printable characters is cut to 64
preconditions: Harness built
expected: Parser receives 64 characters (the parser then rejects it as longer than 48)
evidence: T7: 64 characters passed to the parser
